meta.description: Excited-state (stepwise / cumulative ionization) rate data for a high-pressure (5-15 bar, Tg = 300 K) electron-avalanche model in pure He, Ar and N2, mean electron energy ~4-8 eV (E/N 15-100 Td). Complements ground-state LXCat (IST-Lisbon) cross sections already in use. Targeted (non-systematic) compilation.
sources_searched: LXCat (nl.lxcat.net contributor/database listings; data pages are POST/Cloudflare-driven and could not be read)
LoKI-Suite/LoKI-GM GitHub repository (IST-Lisbon input files, raw text)
IOPscience (open-access HTML of Stankov et al. 2022)
arXiv API, arXiv HTML and ar5iv
meta.access_limitations: LXCat data tables (TRINITI Ar*, He*; BSR Ar(1s) sets) could not be downloaded (session/POST + Cloudflare). NIFS-DATA-059 (Ralchenko He cross sections) is a scanned PDF, not machine-readable. Primary papers (Kolts & Setser 1978, Keto 1974, Vriens & Smeets 1980, Hyman 1979, Blagoev 1979, Lukac 2011, Piper 1988, Holstein 1951, Walsh 1959, MacDonald 1966 book, Raizer 1991 book) were NOT opened; values attributed to them are read from open secondary compilations. OpenAlex and Crossref were intermittently rate-limited (HTTP 429).
meta.verified_flag_meaning: verified=true: the number/expression was read today in the cited accessible source (location in notes). 'access' gives the level: FT = full text of the cited source; FT-2 = full text of an open secondary compilation that attributes the value to a primary not opened; ABS = abstract only; DB = database/repository file read; CALC = my arithmetic from verified inputs (not a published number). verified=false: value not read in an accessible source today (pointer only, or carried from an earlier workspace review, or not found).
meta.units_convention: SI unless stated: two-body m^3/s, three-body m^6/s, radiative s^-1, cross sections m^2, energies eV. Expressions are Python: variables Te_eV, Te_K (=Te_eV*11604.5), Tg_K, d_m (gap width, m), R_m (radius, m). 'Te' in compiled sources is 2/3 of the mean energy; for your two-term EEDFs (mean energy 4-8 eV -> 'Te' ~2.7-5.3 eV) prefer cross sections integrated over your EEDF; Maxwellian fits are given for cross-checking only.
meta.number_density_note: N(300 K) = 2.414e25 m^-3 per bar (CALC, ideal gas). 5 bar: 1.21e26; 10 bar: 2.41e26; 15 bar: 3.62e26 m^-3.
meta.uncertainty_factor_meaning: Multiplicative factor (k_true within k/f..k*f). 'uncertainty_basis' says whether it is stated by a source ('stated'), the spread between independent compilations ('spread'), or my judgement ('estimate').

species_rates.notes: LoKI-GM omits N2(A) + N2(X,v=0) quenching entirely but includes N2(A) + N2(X,v=5-10) -> N2(B) + N2(X,v=0) at 2e-17 m^3/s. Main N2(A) loss at 5-15 bar on ns-us timescales (inference): e-impact (superelastic, ionization, A->B/C), A+A pooling once [A] > ~1e20 m^-3, impurity quenching (O2 etc., not verified here); N2-collisional and radiative loss are slow.

breakdown_comparisons.citation: Park J, Henins I, Herrmann H W, Selwyn G S 2001, Gas breakdown in an atmospheric pressure radio-frequency capacitive plasma source, J. Appl. Phys. 89
breakdown_comparisons.gases: He; He with Ar, O2 or N2 added
breakdown_comparisons.conditions: 13.56 MHz (and frequency variation), atmospheric pressure, capacitive parallel plates
breakdown_comparisons.finding: Breakdown voltage roughly follows a Paschen pd scaling at 13.56 MHz but varies with RF frequency because the electron loss mechanism changes; adding Ar, O2 or N2 to He strongly increases the breakdown voltage despite their lower ionization potentials.
breakdown_comparisons.relevance: Atmospheric-pressure RF He vs He/Ar breakdown; does not isolate stepwise ionization.

breakdown_comparisons.citation: Moravej M et al. 2004, Physics of high-pressure helium and argon radio-frequency plasmas, J. Appl. Phys. 96(12), 7011-7017
breakdown_comparisons.conditions: 50-760 Torr RF discharge with perforated metal electrodes
breakdown_comparisons.finding: Trace impurities did not change the I-V curve shape. Calculated (energy-balance) Te rose with decreasing pressure from 1.1 to 2.4 eV (He) and 1.1 to 2.0 eV (Ar); calculated n_e at 138 mA/cm2: 1.7e11-9.3e11 cm^-3 (He), 2.5e11-2.4e12 cm^-3 (Ar); at 760 Torr Ar n_e was 2.5x He.
breakdown_comparisons.relevance: Sustained (not breakdown) He vs Ar comparison near 1 atm; Te and n_e are model-derived, not measured.

breakdown_comparisons.citation: Jovanovic A P, Hoder T, Hoeft H, Loffhagen D, Becker M M 2023, Formation mechanisms of striations in a filamentary dielectric barrier discharge in atmospheric-pressure argon, Plasma Sources Sci. Technol. 32, 055011
breakdown_comparisons.conditions: 1 atm, 300 K, 1.5 mm single-filament DBD, 60 kHz sine, 1.3 kV amplitude (model)
breakdown_comparisons.finding: Model: stepwise ionization of metastable Ar and ionization of Ar2* excimers are the main electron sources during the transient glow phase that forms striations.
breakdown_comparisons.relevance: Demonstrates (in a model, compared with experiments) that cumulative ionization matters in atmospheric Ar once excited-state densities build up; not a breakdown-field measurement.

breakdown_comparisons.citation: MacDonald A D, Brown S C 1949, High frequency gas discharge breakdown in helium, Phys. Rev. 75, 411-418
breakdown_comparisons.conditions: microwave cavities, wide pressure range (diffusion-controlled breakdown)
breakdown_comparisons.finding: Measured microwave breakdown fields in He vs pressure for several cavity sizes (abstract level).
breakdown_comparisons.relevance: Classic He microwave breakdown benchmark; mostly below 1 atm.
breakdown_comparisons.access: ABS in workspace review experimental-data-krasik-leopold.md (not re-read today)

breakdown_comparisons.citation: Dutton J, Powell D B 1971, J. Phys. B 4, 1506-1515
breakdown_comparisons.finding: alpha/N depends on N at fixed E/N, consistent with Penning ionization of ~1 vpm impurity (abstract level).
breakdown_comparisons.relevance: Shows density-dependent cumulative (metastable-mediated) ionization in He at low E/N.

breakdown_comparisons.citation: MacDonald A D 1966, Microwave Breakdown in Gases (Wiley); Raizer Yu P 1991, Gas Discharge Physics (Springer)

meta.purpose: Evidence to bound a wall-photoemission (gamma_ph) feedback channel in a 4.5-21.7 bar RF cavity with Cu walls: Ar2* second continuum (~126-128 nm, ~9.7-9.8 eV), He2* continuum (~60-100 nm, centred ~80 nm), He 58.4 nm resonance line.
sources_searched: arXiv API + arXiv/ar5iv HTML + arXiv PDFs rendered as text via r.jina.ai (public arXiv PDFs only)
Optica landing page (bot-blocked after first screen)
HAL API (PDF behind an anti-bot wall; not circumvented)
meta.access_limitations: Not opened: Cairns & Samson 1966 full text (Optica, closed + bot wall); Phelps & Petrovic 1999 full text (IOP, closed; abstract only); Feuerbacher & Fitton 1972 full text; Escada/Coelho/Dias Monte Carlo and measurement papers for pure Ar/Xe (abstracts only); Robert et al. 2022 full text (HAL PDF behind Anubis anti-bot page); Thomson, Loeb, Theobald, Raizer books/papers; NIST ASD line query failed (parameter error) so line wavelengths below are CALC from verified level energies.
meta.labels: FT = read in full text of the cited source; FT-2 = read in an open secondary source that cites the primary; ABS = abstract only; CALC = my arithmetic; INF = inference, not a published number.
meta.key_conclusion_INF: Only one quantitative Cu yield was verified: ~10% at 80 nm (He2* continuum), quoted from Cairns & Samson by Aulchenko et al. 2003. No verified Cu yield at 9-10 eV (Ar2* continuum) was found; one source states it is 'considerably reduced' at 150 nm relative to 80 nm. No verified gamma_ph or back-diffusion factor for Ar or He at 15-100 Td was found. High-pressure GEM experiments directly observed photon feedback from a Cu cathode in He at 5 atm (gain > 1e4) but not in Kr; in Ar they report gain limits attributed to other mechanisms.

items.quantity: Quantum efficiency of a Cu photocathode at ~80 nm (He2* continuum, ~15.5 eV)
items.conditions: Cu cathode in a high-pressure GEM vessel; value quoted as 'about 10%' (surface state not specified; presumably air-exposed technical Cu); original measurement Cairns & Samson 1966 (untreated metal foils)
items.uncertainty_basis: Cairns & Samson abstract: untreated photocathodes usable as secondary standards with probable uncertainty ~+/-30% over 400-1100 A
items.citation: Aulchenko V et al. 2003, Further studies of GEM performance in dense noble gases, Nucl. Instrum. Meth. A 513, 256-259 (arXiv:physics/0211101), Sec. 2; citing Cairns R B, Samson J A R 1966, J. Opt. Soc. Am. 56, 1568
items.notes: Same paper: 'the quantum efficiency of Cu is considerably reduced at the emission region of Kr (150 nm)' - no number. Cairns & Samson abstract (ABS) confirms Cu was among 18 metals measured over 200-1200 A (10.3-62 eV) and gives the +/-30% figure; the Cu values themselves were not read. 80 nm is inside the requested 12-21 eV range; the yield at 58.4 nm (21.2 eV) and at 9.8 eV was not verified.

items.quantity: Cu yield at ~126-128 nm (9.7-9.8 eV), clean vs oxidized
items.citation: NOT FOUND in an accessible source. Qualitative only: Lux T 2019 JINST 14 P03006 (arXiv:1812.08700), Sec. 7: Ar S2 photons (128 +/- 10 nm, 8-12 eV) lie far above the Cu vacuum work function of about 4.5 eV, so Cu photoemission feedback is plausible in pure Ar.
items.notes: Primary candidates not opened: Cairns & Samson 1966 (Cu, 200-1200 A); Phelps & Petrovic 1999 review of vuv-photon yields (abstract says yields 'vary greatly with particle energy and surface condition'). Feuerbacher & Fitton 1972 (J. Appl. Phys. 43, 1563, doi 10.1063/1.1661362) does NOT include Cu: its abstract lists Au, Al, stainless steel, vitreous carbon, Aquadag, graphite, silica, In2O3, up to 25 eV. No oxidized-Cu data found. Treat Y_Cu(9.8 eV) as a free parameter; the only verified constraint is Y(150 nm) << Y(80 nm) ~ 0.1.

items.topic: 2 Back-diffusion / backscattering of photoelectrons in dense gas
items.quantity: Extraction efficiency f = (photocurrent in gas)/(photocurrent in vacuum at same field)
items.conditions: CsI photocathode, ~800 Torr, E/p 0-3 V cm^-1 Torr^-1 (about 0-9 Td, CALC: 1 V/cm/Torr = 3.03 Td at 293 K); Monte Carlo studies for Xe, Ar, Ne at E/N < 40 Td and photon energies 6.7-9.8 eV
items.citation: Escada J et al. 2009 JINST 4 P11025 (arXiv:0909.2965), Introduction and Sec. 4 (FT); Dias T H V T et al. 2003, 'Dependence of the photoelectron collection efficiency in noble gases on the incident VUV photon energy', IEEE NSS 2002 (doi 10.1109/NSSMIC.2002.1239387) abstract (ABS); Escada J et al. 2007 JINST 2 P08001 abstract (ABS); Buzulutskov A 2002 NIM A 494, 148 (arXiv:physics/0206082) Sec. 2 (FT); Phelps A V, Petrovic Z Lj 1999 PSST 8 R21 abstract (ABS)
items.notes: Verified trends: backscattering to the photocathode is 'particularly significant in noble gases' because of strong low-energy elastic scattering (Escada 2009, FT); f rises with E/p, fastest at low fields (FT); in Xe, Ar and Ne the collection probability rises with E/N and falls with increasing photon energy over 6.7-9.8 eV (Dias 2003, ABS); molecular additives raise f (FT). Phelps & Petrovic 1999 review corrections for non-equilibrium electron motion near the cathode (ABS) but no number was read. No numerical f for pure Ar or He at 15-100 Td, nor for metal (Cu) cathodes, was read. Thomson/Loeb/Theobald back-diffusion formulas: not accessed.

items.topic: 3 Measured photon feedback, He vs heavier gases at high pressure
items.quantity: Photon-feedback secondary signal relative to primary avalanche signal, Cu cathode, pure He
items.conditions: Pure He, 5 atm, room temperature; feedback between last GEM and Cu cathode; GEM optical transparency ~10% each; visible only at gains > ~1e4; absent in Kr at 2 atm (gain 4e3); super-exponential gain in He above 1e5
items.citation: Aulchenko V et al. 2003 NIM A 513, 256 (arXiv:physics/0211101), Sec. 2 and Fig. 1
items.notes: Authors attribute the feedback to He VUV emission centred at 80 nm, with a characteristic emission time of order 1 us in a discharge (citing Huffman, Larrabee, Tanaka 1965 JOSA 55, 101). This is direct evidence that He2* VUV feedback from Cu is significant at several atm, with a microsecond delay.

items.topic: 3 Gain limits vs pressure in pure noble gases (Cu-clad GEMs)
items.conditions: Pure gases, 99.99%, 1-15 atm, room temperature, X-ray irradiation
items.uncertainty_basis: stated (gain uncertainty within a factor of 2)
items.citation: Bondar A et al. 2002 NIM A 493, 8 (arXiv:physics/0204054) Secs. 3-6 (FT); Bondar A, Buzulutskov A, Shekhtman L 2002 NIM A 481, 200 (arXiv:physics/0103082) abstract (ABS); Buzulutskov A 2002 NIM A 494, 148 (arXiv:physics/0206082) Secs. 3-4 (FT)
items.notes: The authors attribute the heavy-gas gain limit to ion feedback (ion-induced emission from GEM electrodes), not photon feedback, and the light-gas behaviour to associative ionization (He + He* -> He2+ + e), estimated at ~2/3 of ionization in He at 1 atm and dominant at higher pressure (Buzulutskov 2002, FT). Relevant to your earlier He low-field question: alpha/p in He and Ne at 1-15 atm was much larger than low-pressure values and violated E/p scaling. The journal DOI for Buzulutskov 2002 was not looked up; the arXiv link is given instead.

items.value: G_tot = G_av + eps_ph2ch * G_ph / (1 - p*G_ph); stability requires p*G < 1
items.conditions: LEM/THGEM in pure Ar, 90 K, 760 Torr (simulation) and 2.5 bar Ar/Xe data from the literature
items.citation: Lux T 2019 JINST 14 P03006 (arXiv:1812.08700), Sec. 7, Eqs. 7.1-7.3 and Fig. 7b
items.notes: Lux argues from over-exponential measured gain curves that photon feedback contributes in pure Ar (more than in Xe, whose photons are 7.2 eV). Simulation: fewer than 1% of electron-gas interactions are ionizations, so each avalanche electron is accompanied by >100 excitations/VUV photons at these fields (model result, Fig. 7b). No fitted p or Cu yield is given in the text read.

items.topic: 3/4 Excimer VUV photoemission at atmospheric pressure in Ar
items.quantity: Role of Ar2* VUV-induced secondary emission
items.conditions: Ar-NH3 Penning mixture plane-plane DBD, 1 atm, LF 50 kHz and dual LF-RF (5 MHz); TDLAS of Ar(1s3) with a 1D fluid model
items.citation: Robert R, Hagelaar G, Sadeghi N, Magnan R, Stafford L, Massines F 2022, Role of excimer formation and induced photoemission on the Ar metastable kinetics in atmospheric pressure Ar-NH3 dielectric barrier discharges, Plasma Sources Sci. Technol. 31, 065010
items.notes: The abstract states that the model only matched measured sub-microsecond Ar(1s) rise/decay after adding fast Ar2* formation and VUV emission; that in media optically thin for these photons they readily reach the barriers/electrodes and induce secondary emission; and that this photoemission plays a significant role in the metastable kinetics, the dominant ionization pathways and the alpha-gamma transition. The photoemission yield used was not read (full text not accessible).

items.quantity: Yields of electrons per vuv photon at metal cathodes; fitted breakdown model 15 Td-100 kTd
items.conditions: Ar, low-current cold-cathode discharges and breakdown
items.citation: Phelps A V, Petrovic Z Lj 1999, Cold-cathode discharges and breakdown in argon: surface and gas phase production of secondary electrons, Plasma Sources Sci. Technol. 8, R21
items.notes: Abstract read: the review correlates electron yields per ion, fast atom, metastable and vuv photon (which 'vary greatly with particle energy and surface condition') and fits breakdown and maintenance data over 15 Td-100 kTd. No numerical gamma_ph or back-diffusion factor was read. This is the most important source to obtain for bounding Ar.

items.topic: 4 Delays / jitter from VUV or metastable wall feedback

value.He_VUV_feedback_delay: order 1 us (He discharge emission time; observed secondary pulses)

items.citation: Aulchenko 2003 (FT); Ar2-radiative entry in species_rates (Stankov 2022, Millet 1982, Amsler 2008, Santorelli 2021); Markovic V Lj et al. 2005, Explanation of the memory effect in argon, Facta Universitatis Ser. Phys. Chem. Technol. 3(2), 95-107 (ABS)
items.notes: No study was found that directly compares formative-delay or jitter distributions in Ar vs He attributable to VUV photoemission. Markovic 2005 (ABS, low pressure) attributes the long-time 'memory effect' in Ar breakdown delay to Ar2+ afterglow decay (up to hundreds of ms) and then N-atom surface recombination/field emission, not to metastables, which are quenched. INF: because ~half or more of Ar2* and the He2* VUV are emitted on a ~1-3 us scale, a photoemission feedback loop would add secondary avalanches delayed by microseconds, which broadens formative delay distributions if the primary avalanche gain is near threshold.

items.topic: 5 Transmission of Ar2* continuum through Ar
items.citation: Santorelli R et al. 2021 EPJC (arXiv:2012.08262), second-continuum light detected through Ar gas at 1.5-16 bar (FT); Robert et al. 2022 abstract: Ar media optically thin for Ar2* VUV (ABS); Stankov 2022 Table 1 levels for CALC
items.notes: CALC: Ar ground-state resonance absorption lies at 1239.84/11.624 = 106.7 nm (1s4) and 1239.84/11.828 = 104.8 nm (1s2), about 1.8-2 eV above the 126 nm continuum photon energy, so only far-wing/collision-induced absorption by ground-state Ar is possible; no measured coefficient at 126 nm and 5-20 bar was found. Unverified attenuation sources: absorption by excited species (Ar*, Ar2*) at high excitation density and by impurities (O2, H2O, hydrocarbons) - treat as model parameters.

items.topic: 5 Transmission of He2* continuum and He 58.4 nm line through He
items.value: He2* continuum (~60-100 nm) transmitted over mm-cm at several atm (qualitative); He 58.4 nm resonance radiation strongly self-absorbed (INF)
items.citation: Aulchenko 2003 (FT): 80 nm He emission reached the Cu cathode through the GEM gaps at 5 atm and produced feedback; IE(He) = 24.587 eV from NIST ASD (verified in workspace review gas-kinetics-coefficients.md) for CALC
items.notes: CALC: the He photoionization edge is 1239.84/24.587 = 50.4 nm; photons longward of the 58.4 nm (21.2 eV) resonance line cannot be absorbed by ground-state He except in pressure-broadened line wings (INF). The 58.4 nm line itself is a resonance line of the ground state, so at 5-22 bar it is trapped and converted (via He(2^1P) collisions/three-body processes) rather than reaching the wall directly (INF; the 58.4 nm wavelength and its oscillator strength were not re-verified because the NIST line query failed). No measured He2*-continuum absorption coefficient in dense He was read.

items.quantity: Effective photon feedback coefficient per avalanche ionization
items.value: gamma_ph_eff = (n_exc/n_ion) * eta_VUV * Omega_wall * T_gas * Y_Cu(E_ph) * f_bd(E/N)
items.conditions: Townsend-type self-sustainment when gamma_ph_eff*(exp(alpha*d) - 1) >= 1 (same structure as Lux Eq. 7.1, p*G < 1 for stability)
items.citation: INF/CALC built from verified pieces: n_exc/n_ion > 100 in Ar at LEM fields (Lux 2019, simulation); Y_Cu(80 nm) ~ 0.1 (Aulchenko/Cairns & Samson); f_bd < 1 and rising with E/N (Escada 2009, Dias 2003); T_gas ~ 1 for Ar2* in Ar and He2* in He (qualitative)
items.notes: Your BOLSIG/LXCat runs give n_exc/n_ion at 15-100 Td directly. eta_VUV (fraction of excitations ending as wall-reaching VUV) at 5-22 bar is close to 1 in Ar (rapid Ar2* formation, see Ar-excimer-formation-time) minus quenching by impurities; Omega_wall is geometric (up to ~0.5 for a planar wall). Unbounded pieces: Y_Cu(9.8 eV) for Ar and f_bd at 15-100 Td for both gases. A sensitivity sweep over Y_Cu*f_bd from 1e-4 to 1e-1 is recommended rather than a single value.
